title: Best Practices?
author: Reign2294
selftext:
Hi there! Long time lurker here. 

I have been working on two projects recently, but have been wondering about some of the systems level setups everyone is using and whether I am doing something big-brained or just whacking my keyboard with a stick. I am using Claude Code with a system that utilizes API model query for single point tasks like testing, writing, reading. 

1) Continual work: So, I would like my main context to be working at all hours and just reserving design and game system questions for me when I have time, which is usually after the kids sleep. I found it quickly would stop itself on a question, only for me to agree with it, so I built an "infer from my previous decision rule" which helped a bit but I found it slowing work often for other reasons like what it believed was low context. I ended up building a "heartbeat" system that basically injected a "how's it going" prompt every 30 minutes to assure the agent was continually working. It works decently now, especially since I have repeatedly underscored an outgoing agent minimum, but I am unsure if this is the best way. 

2) Context and Handovers: I knew about handovers pretty early, but was always doing it manually. I only recently was able to setup the infamous auto-compact with a hook that could get an injection prompt timed for after the compact occurred. I queued this at 70% context. Issue was, I wanted things like logs saved, handover built, git commit, save of folder state to another drive (paranoid), etc etc. So, I queued that to occur at 60% context, with a note to include work that was done after in the injection prompt so the next session could be aware of what was unsaved. Again, this sort of works now, but I occasionally find the new sessions somewhat lobotomized despite multiple fable-level reviews into my handover system. Anyone have better luck here? 

3) Context Efficiency: I found out pretty early that having one main context agent managing and doing all the delegation was making context fill up 2-3x daily. I managed this first by building a system that sent vision tasks to Deepseek V4 flash or Gemini vision models. I had testing sometimes done by Kimi K3 and Qwen. All of that helped, but I was marginal. My weekly context with Anthropic was doing fine thanks to the API delegation, but my main agent context was still hitting compact too often. I ended up working on building a department lead system with the elevation to delegate to anthropic and API models themselves. This was a juggle to assure they had the right context about the project and could act on the road map we had in place. However, once it started working I found a 3-4x improvement in the rate of which main session context was filling. This has been one of the largest upgrades to our context, but i am still early development in the Godot game I am building so I am unsure if there is a better practice out there. Any thoughts? 

4) Learning loops: This is the newest section for me, but it was a Hail-Mary attempt at building a way for the main session context and the Department Leads could get better and more context-efficient and smarter over time. My issue was that I was finding the delegators were trying to provide resources, background info, and ruling context from the game to the agents they were delegating work to, but often missing or sending way more than needed, obviously costing money. I have been trying (with limited success) to build a system that has files for all delegators where they can basically add a tick (counter) for each time their agents they delegate to use a reference beit rulings or whatever. The idea is that after 10 passes, any reference item that has been sent out (now deemed unused by the agents it was sent to) is no longer sent to them. If agents find they need more context or rulings, they request them, and they're added to the list to be reviewed after 10 turns, if that makes sense. This idea is really new toc me andf likely hobbled together, but perhaps you guys have other ideas or best-practices? 

Anyways, I am doing all this to learn, and it has been a load of fun. I once had the agent send me 107 open questions and ramifications it needed me to answer to move forwards after one 10 hour night session.... needless to say, I quickly made the change to promote the main session to CEO basically saying I was founder and only wanteRd 10-20 questions daily, ideally already passed to see if I have answered them before or whether they could be answered by a team who had access to my previous rulings and could infer new rulings on my behalf.

 Eh, it's been a long journey and I have only been messing around for 2 months. Any resources or best-practices you all can recommend at a systems level? I am a writer and gamer, not a coder or game developer, but I figured I could learn much if I set my mind to it and used these tools to the best of their ability. :) 

Would love any ideas or feedback!

comments.author: Popular_Procedure_84
comments.body: Don't know, but I would love to learn some too.
